feature_name: Materialized views over Apache Iceberg tables
summary: BigQuery can create materialized views over Apache Iceberg tables when the view is partition-aligned with the base table using time-based partition transformations.
extended_definition: BigQuery can create materialized views over Apache Iceberg tables when the view is partition-aligned with the base table using time-based partition transformations.

supporting_pages.title: "Introduction to BigLake external tables \_|\_ BigQuery \_|\_ Google Cloud\
evidence_snippets: These materialized views function like materialized views over BigQuery-managed storage tables, including the benefits of automatic refresh and smart tuning .

Cache-enabled tables with materialized views You can use materialized views over BigLake metadata cache-enabled tables to improve performance and efficiency when querying structured data stored in Cloud Storage or Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3).

BigLake tables support the following formats: Avro CSV Delta Lake Iceberg JSON ORC Parquet You can't use cached metadata with Apache Iceberg external tables ; BigQuery already uses the metadata that Iceberg captures in manifest files.

supporting_pages.title: Create and use tables \_|\_ BigQuery \_|\_ Google Cloud Documentation
evidence_snippets: To see the exact permissions that are required, expand the Required permissions section: Required permissions The following permissions are required to create a table: bigquery.tables.create on the dataset where you're creating the table. bigquery.tables.getData on all tables and views that your query references if you're saving query results as a table. bigquery.jobs.create on the project if you're creating the table by loading data or by saving query results to a table. bigquery.tables.updateData on the table if you're appending to or overwriting a table with query results.
